## Changes since `v0.6.0`

### Features

- search the current folder and every folder under it by file name from the SFTP drawer: the filter only looked at the folder on screen, so finding a config or log somewhere in a tree meant opening folder after folder or running find in the terminal; the search box gains a subfolders option that searches on Enter with the filter's own matching (text, glob, or a regular expression that falls back to a glob, ignoring case) and the hidden-files setting, and the results replace the listing with each one's folder beside its name, can be opened, downloaded, renamed, compressed, deleted or shown in their folder, and stream in under a strip that tells the count and can stop the search; the server's find walks the tree where it lives, named on a command channel of the pooled connection and prefiltered with -iname where that cannot drop a match, and a host that cannot run it, such as a Windows server or an SFTP-only account, is searched over SFTP several folders at a time without following links, skipping folders it cannot read; a search stops at 1000 matches and when its query is cleared or another folder opens ([cbbfd7f2](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cbbfd7f2df9067443396174da6ecc8b16b8aca64))
- compress entries and extract archives on the server from the SFTP drawer: packing a folder to download it, or unpacking an upload where it landed, meant leaving for the terminal, and SFTP can only move bytes; the context menu gains Compress… for the row or selection, which asks for a name and tar.gz, zip, tar.xz, tar.bz2 or tar, and Extract… for tar archives of any common compression, zip, 7z and single .gz, .bz2 or .xz files, which asks where (a folder named after the archive by default, created when missing) and whether to replace existing files; the work runs as tar, zip, unzip, 7z or gzip over a command channel of the tab's pooled connection, with the script sent to sh on standard input so the login shell's quoting never applies, and shows in the transfers panel, where cancelling sends SIGTERM so the command stops on the host and a half-written archive is removed; a missing tool is named, an existing archive is never overwritten, and items from different folders are refused ([00ef1feb](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/00ef1feb3146c1d048a0cd14caf23b3e45e05fe1))
- choose a connection's keyword highlight set in the connection dialog: profiles could keep a set but nothing let the user pick one; SSH and serial connections get a Keyword highlighting field that follows the default set, names a set or turns highlighting off, and a set deleted since shows as the default set, which the terminal falls back to as well ([7567fff8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/7567fff88900b8e8baf1c536a9e488fe926b9d3d))
- add a Highlighting settings page for keyword highlight sets: the rules had no place to be seen or changed; the page turns highlighting on or off, picks the default set and whether full-screen programs are highlighted, and edits the sets: add, copy, rename and delete sets, restore the built-in rules, and add, order, toggle and edit rules with their match type, case, whole word and colors from the theme's palette or a custom one; a pattern is saved once valid, with the error shown while typing, and a preview colors sample output, or the user's own, as the set would; each edit builds on the one before it is saved, since settings are saved whole ([1170476f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/1170476f9457a92e19766cbc4a6c4560c1d12523))
- highlight keywords in terminal output as it appears: with the sets in place, terminals color what they match without the user searching for it; each terminal loads a KeywordHighlighter addon that colors matches with xterm decorations, so copied text, logs and searches still see the output as sent, and only the lines on screen and a screen around them carry decorations, matched again only when their text changes, so a flood of output or a long scrollback costs no more; full-screen programs are left alone unless the setting asks, a hidden tab catches up when shown, the colors follow the connection's theme, and the terminal's context menu can pause highlighting for that tab ([400c0f9c](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/400c0f9c615b1756c622f882fcf80427d10a9511))
- keep keyword highlight sets in the config and let connections pick one: the sets need to be saved, synced and backed up like other settings, and a connection to a switch wants other rules than one to a web server; the config gains keyword_highlight (on or off, the default set, whether full-screen programs are highlighted, and the sets, unset while the built-in set applies so its rules improve with tTerm), synced across devices, and SSH and serial profiles a highlight_set that names a set or off and follows the default set when unset, which an ssh_config import keeps ([0efa0ae0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/0efa0ae0fc8066d06a1492c958bc2946ccdacae0))
- match keywords in terminal text for highlighting: operators and network engineers rely on Xshell's highlight sets and SecureCRT's keyword highlighting to spot error, denied or an IP address in a flood of output, and tTerm had nothing like it; src/lib/keywordHighlight holds named sets of keyword or regex rules with optional case and whole-word matching and a text and background color each, a palette color name that follows the terminal theme or a hex color, a built-in set (errors, warnings, successes, IPv4, IPv6 that needs a digit so Add::add stays plain, MAC addresses), the matching that lets the earlier rule win where matches overlap and caps the text and highlights per line, and the reading of buffer rows into text with the cell behind each character, wrapped rows and wide characters included, skipping cells the program colored itself ([580758f3](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/580758f35cf78617c135dd0896a7f27a17d52f9a))
- take the terminal to a folder from the SFTP drawer: going the other way, from a folder found in the file panel to a shell in it, meant copying the path and typing cd; the drawer's header gets a button for the listed folder and a folder's context menu an "Open in Terminal" item, which type cd with the path escaped at this tab's prompt (not at the tabs it broadcasts to) and show the terminal, and say the terminal is busy instead while an editor, a pager or a command shell integration saw start has it ([462edfa5](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/462edfa5a4d14c0f80afab1288480e41284c7ad6))
- let the SFTP drawer open at home, the last directory or the terminal's directory, and follow the terminal: users cd in the terminal and expect the file panel to go along, as FinalShell, MobaXterm and Xshell do, but the drawer ignored what remote shells report and always resumed the last directory; a new SFTP setting picks where drawers open (the last directory stays the default, so nothing changes until it is set), a connection can choose otherwise, and a toggle in the drawer follows each directory the shell reports with OSC 7, on from the start for drawers that open at the terminal's directory; remote reports go to a store of their own so they never reach the local tab's restart directory, a directory SFTP cannot list falls back to where the drawer opens otherwise and is not retried, a hidden drawer catches up when shown, and the toggle says when the shell reports nothing because the connection lacks Shell integration ([a9a8f689](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/a9a8f6890c40486d33972d21a6c088db50e47530))
- report the remote shell's directory even with command marks off: the SFTP drawer is going to follow the terminal's directory, which the remote scripts already report (OSC 7) at every prompt, but turning Mark commands off in Settings skipped installing them altogether; the install now goes ahead and starts the shell with tterm_marks=0, so it only reports the directory, and the "marks off" reason goes away; the scripts to paste into ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc or config.fish report the directory too ([224cf07a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/224cf07aa49ba33f3196d96cd228483223d441c2))
- make the title bar transfers button say what is moving: its icon was always the download arrow, even with only uploads queued, and a spinner replaced it while anything ran; it now shows the upload, download, delete or both-ways icon for the active transfers (the history when none is active), rings the icon with the share of bytes moved, and counts the active transfers, the failed ones once idle, or all of them; it also gets the aria-label and tooltip it lacked ([bf35df3b](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bf35df3b4ddddca16ab8b2f99412b9b8b2c41b5f))
- let a serial connection complete the line breaks its device sends only half of: a new "Received newlines" choice beside "Enter sends" turns a lone CR or a lone LF into CRLF, for devices that echo Enter as a CR alone and leave the cursor at the start of the same line, or print a staircase with LFs alone; a break split across two reads is completed once, a run of CRs such as \\r\\r\\n stays one break, the screen, timestamps and the session log get the completed text while the hex view keeps the bytes sent, and file transfers are untouched ([5f76ce97](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/5f76ce975f69554f10519202fdadc7bb288126fe))
- keep a serial send bar's history in the database instead of the browser, so it syncs and goes into backups with the command library, and let it be cleared: a history menu beside the input puts a send back, removes one or clears the connection's; a send made on two devices stays one record with the later time, a profile's history goes with the profile, each connection keeps its newest 30, and only the show-sends choice stays per device ([09ad5f21](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/09ad5f2149c8e5c99fcf62d006e7a6f7143f6bff))
- show an XMODEM receive, whose sender gives no size, as bytes arriving instead of a stuck 0%: the start event marks the size unknown and the transfer row shows a pulsing bar, the bytes and speed, and the bytes received once done ([879b0f5b](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/879b0f5b8c8c5fdb15ff3c46e8d91d5175d5106e))
- receive files from a serial device over XMODEM, XMODEM-1K or YMODEM: the send bar saves XMODEM's one file where asked and YMODEM's into a folder under the names the device gives, kept inside it and numbered when taken; the receiver asks with C, falls back to checksums for old XMODEM senders, asks again for broken blocks, skips repeated ones, trims XMODEM's padding and cuts YMODEM's files to their size, deletes a half-written file when the transfer fails, and shares the port claim, transfer rows and cancel with sending ([912cc5c5](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/912cc5c5bc2535512494dc9e7968b0ce7dd9fd51))
- show what a serial send bar sends and keep what it sent: each send can appear in the terminal as a cyan line after an arrow, as text with its control characters visible or as the hex bytes, on a line of its own and timed when timestamps are on, and the history and that choice are kept per saved connection, or per port for an unsaved one ([66fd85f5](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/66fd85f5a231a9cf9876b2fdbcd20142b78e0c05))
- send files to a serial device over XMODEM, XMODEM-1K or YMODEM, as bootloaders take firmware: the send bar picks the protocol and the files, and while the transfer runs the port's input goes to it instead of the terminal and typing is held back, as during ZMODEM, whose transfer rows and cancel it shares; the sender waits up to a minute for the device to ask, follows CRC or checksum as asked, resends refused blocks, sends YMODEM's names and sizes, and gives up after ten tries or when the device cancels ([252b9f2e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/252b9f2eac42be721fbd1bd1ae1e09a03af9081a))
- send text or hex from a serial tab's send bar: text goes out as typing does, with the line ending and charset, and hex bytes as they are through write_serial_bytes, with Enter's bytes added when asked; Enter sends, the arrow keys go through what was sent, and a send can repeat every so many milliseconds until stopped or it fails ([c32836ff](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c32836ffbedfea5a4d7fddc78d363dee36975893))
- show what a serial device sends in hex: a HEX button on the serial bar, or the connection's own default, turns received bytes into lines of sixteen, with a new line after each pause so every frame starts one and timestamps mark it; the backend makes the hex from the bytes as sent, keeps logging the decoded text, and keeps the view across reconnects ([054bc297](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/054bc297b5528ecad68a944163673c52d583fff0))
- talk to a serial device in its own charset: a serial connection picks one of the charsets SSH offers, and its output is decoded to UTF-8 and logged so, through an output filter the reader thread now takes, while typed text goes out in that charset after Enter becomes the chosen line ending; the encoding field the SSH form had moves into EncodingField for both forms ([bd8e0328](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bd8e03286e85570eeedc53d19bbfa5721ed2b0e0))
- open serial connections from the connection dialog: a third type picks a port from the ones this machine lists, with its USB device, or one typed by name, and sets the baud rate, framing, flow control, what Enter sends, local echo and timestamps; saved ones show in the profiles, the settings and the new-tab launcher with a USB icon, and their tabs open with a header that names the port and its settings and toggles DTR and RTS, pulses RTS to reset a board, sends a break, turns timestamps and local echo on and off, and says while the device is unplugged that it is waited for ([971e57cd](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/971e57cd7bb3e1a49194c3ce496acff5154644bd))
- open serial ports as a third kind of session: a serial connection names its port, baud rate, framing, flow control and what Enter sends, and its tab reads and writes the port through the same reader thread, input queue, ZMODEM and session log as a local shell; list_serial_ports names each port's USB device, set_serial_signals, pulse_serial_line and send_serial_break drive DTR, RTS and break, and a device that goes away is looked for every half second until it comes back, under its new name if it was replugged, for as long as the tab stays open; the Linux CI and release jobs install libudev-dev, which the serialport crate lists ports with ([c5303588](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c530358848c9f02bc71e27d1ee04b3ab6c670c76))
- keep an SSH tab's icon with its saved connection: the distribution its host runs and the icon picked under Edit Tab are saved in the profile, so its new tabs show them at once and every open tab of it changes together; the connection dialog can pick the icon too, and the saved distribution is dropped once the host or port changes ([fcdca81d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/fcdca81da06302a1563144575b2c5dc43a6e4710))
- show the logo of the Linux distribution an SSH host runs as its tab's icon: once the shell starts, tTerm reads /etc/os-release on a channel of its own, a server until then or for a host without one; the icon picker offers the distribution logos too, SSH tabs can get an icon of their own under Edit Tab, and turning tab icons off also stops the check ([f5eed87a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f5eed87a80efebfed1ae2f76b4d9666476128b66))
- let the badge a tab shows for an AI agent take a chosen style and color: seven animations while it works (half disc, ring, comet, orbit, pulse, dots, braille) and three marks while it waits (pause bars, ring, still pause bars), each in the theme's color or one picked in Settings > Appearance, shown running beside its name; every style animates only transform and opacity so the badges stay on the compositor, and settings sync carries the choice ([0a3e36b9](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/0a3e36b9e3d6bc20604a5299a06b926d90bf2386))
- let notifications play a chosen sound instead of the system's: four built-in tones synthesized in the app (chime, ding, pop, rise) or an audio file of up to 1 MB, since the system sound was unpleasant and a Windows toast plays only the system's sounds for an unpackaged app, so the notification is shown silently and tTerm plays the sound itself on every platform, falling back to the system sound when the file cannot be read or decoded; a picked file is copied into the config folder so it outlives the original, and local and WebDAV backups, their restore snapshots and settings sync carry the copy to other devices ([9e17d02d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9e17d02df429f8f1c3cf1781bc9030a42cd222a2))
- manage the SSH key vault in Settings > Security and pick a vault key in the connection dialog, so a key can be imported once, used by any connection on every synced device and exported back to a key file: the private key field of profiles and jump hosts switches between a key file and the key vault and can save a key file into the vault, and the backup, sync and reset texts now say they cover the vault's keys ([cb685ed2](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cb685ed25db4c25c863df1b8d7e5b31a0bc1144d))
- add an SSH key vault that keeps private keys and their certificates encrypted in the database with the saved passwords, so password sync and encrypted backups take them to other devices instead of leaving profiles pointing at key files that only exist on one machine: a profile signs in with a vault key through the private key path tterm-key:<id>, which key loading, automatic authentication, tunnel credential checks and the missing key file report after a restore all resolve, and new commands import, list, rename, re-certify, delete and export keys, the export asking the user to verify it is them ([e5979595](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e597959593cc5fb68530849348e5427910fdf204))

### Fixes

- keep bash's prompt hook when a profile assigns PROMPT_COMMAND: bash got the hook through the environment before it read the login files, so a ~/.bash_profile or ~/.bashrc with PROMPT_COMMAND="history -a" dropped it, and with it the directory reports the SFTP drawer follows and the command marks; start.sh now runs bash --posix --login, which reads only $ENV, and bash/init.bash leaves POSIX mode, reads the login files in bash's order and then puts the hook first in PROMPT_COMMAND, keeping a login shell and ~/.bash_history; the hook and PROMPT_COMMAND are no longer exported, so a shell started with su does not report its directory; macOS's own bash reads the login files even in POSIX mode and never $ENV, so it keeps the hook up front; the real-shell tests now replace PROMPT_COMMAND in the profile, check the directory report, and cover command marks off ([721e85da](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/721e85da01ceec55db835d05faac3d9ded862d6f))
- connect to servers whose only host key is RSA: russh was built without its rsa feature to keep RUSTSEC-2023-0071 out, so it could not verify RSA host keys and tTerm stopped offering them, which locked out CentOS 6 and much network equipment; that advisory is a timing leak in private-key operations, while checking a host key uses only the server's public key, and tTerm keeps signing with RSA key files through ring, so the feature is now on; RSA stays after Ed25519 and ECDSA so a server with both keeps presenting the key it was trusted with, and SHA-1 ssh-rsa comes last; the explanation for an unverifiable host now names the DSA-only servers it still applies to ([84dbec0b](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/84dbec0b323893df5a411ed88e3fb0b12db1d2f0))
- stop id-less OSC 8 links from piling up while a TUI redraws them: xterm 6 gives every link without an id its own entry and marker, freed only once its line leaves the scrollback, so a link redrawn in place leaked about 3 KB per frame; an id-less link now reuses the entry with the same URI already on that line of the same buffer, installed for terminal tabs and the log replay player ([11ecd9af](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/11ecd9af3c41a9daceee4023fa3436e8ef6ae1b1))
- offer "Edit connection" in a serial tab's context menu: the tab bar and the split group header only offered it to SSH tabs, though a serial tab opened from a saved profile can already be edited and its open tabs updated on save; a serial tab without a profile still gets no item, since saving a connection as a profile only handles SSH ([3960f5c1](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3960f5c1eb0e2b0327f14df2321022887712f20b))
- let a serial tab's HEX button work while its device is unplugged: the view now hangs off the tab's session instead of the open port, so set_serial_view reaches it between attempts and the device comes back in the view chosen ([d39af466](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d39af4669c355c02a436986b6944dde601046f5c))
- show Linux Mint and other derivatives with their own logo: a host's ID and name now win over its ID_LIKE, where Linux Mint names Ubuntu and so showed Ubuntu's logo in the server monitor ([27f10318](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/27f1031861653558a093a3aae6c9058b2343b845))
- turn mouse reporting off once the shell is back at its prompt, since a program killed before it could turn reporting off (Ctrl+C while claude starts) left every mouse move typed into the shell's line editor as text like 35;74;19M: a shell integration prompt mark (OSC 133/633 A) turns it off at once, and on macOS and Linux local tabs, which have no marks by default, the new pty_shell_in_foreground command is asked once output settles whether the shell leads the terminal's foreground process group again, checking the leader is still a shell so an exec'd tmux keeps its reporting ([44361ad0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/44361ad084abf2955262c80d9ac4bfcaed137b60))
- let the settings sidebar scroll when the dialog is too short to show every category, since the aside had no overflow and the categories below the fold were clipped out of reach ([e3e3a63c](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e3e3a63cfcc2427516586f5a33027a64ccd698e2))
- recognize an SFTP drag out dropped on a File Explorer folder whose path is longer than 260 characters, since the shell's create notice was read into a MAX_PATH buffer with SHGetPathFromIDListW and failed for deep folders, so the drop was reported as landing on an unknown target; SHGetPathFromIDListEx now reads it into a buffer sized for the longest path Windows allows ([ede17675](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/ede176759023f3f33af251815a7177d896bfa677))
- have File Explorer show what an SFTP drag out downloaded without a manual refresh, since right after its own copy of the drop placeholders it could miss the file system's notices for the placeholder delete and the download's part file, rename and sidecar delete, leaving stale entries until F5: each deleted placeholder is now announced to the shell with SHCNE_DELETE or SHCNE_RMDIR, and once the download into the dropped-on folder ends, even if it failed, the new refresh_drop_folder command sends SHCNE_UPDATEDIR so the folder is listed again; macOS leaves Finder to follow the folder itself ([bac289a8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bac289a848c40ba248b92d34df650afca1b48c05))

### Performance

- stop typing into a serial port lagging on Windows: the reader no longer waits inside a read for input, which held each keystroke's write back until the read timed out and often won the port again for the next one, so keystrokes went out hundreds of milliseconds late and some seconds late; it asks how much input is waiting, which returns at once, and reads only when there is some, checking every 2 ms, so a write gets the port between checks and a com0com round trip drops from about 230-440 ms to under 3 ms ([9b42d5d6](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9b42d5d6f6e67ebf568c71b9b107233c86509993))

### UI and usability

- name the folder an SFTP drop uploads to: the drop overlay said only "current directory", which is easy to misread with several tabs open, so it now prints the path below the hint, on one line cut at the end with the full path on hover; the arrow also floats gently while files are over the drawer, unless the system asks for reduced motion ([5e48f0c2](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/5e48f0c2df687cdccbd11c5e1cf4906e86656d4d))
- tell transfer rows apart at a glance: upload and download sat in the same gray box with only the arrow differing, so the direction box is now tinted per direction (sky, violet, gray for delete; fixed hues because one theme's primary is green, the color of done) and the status moves onto its corner as a small badge, freeing the right side for the file name; a delete shows Trash2 like the SFTP toolbar, and Remove, which also used Trash2, becomes X; the cancel and remove buttons and the direction box get accessible names ([8dc709b5](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/8dc709b50ba90821a743cc9e2f792595d5b86061))
- draw upload and download with one set of icons: context menus used the Upload and Download tray glyphs while the SFTP toolbar and the transfers panel used ArrowUpFromLine and ArrowDownToLine, so the same action looked different in each place; menus now use the arrows too, an SFTP entry's Download shows FileDown or FolderDown for one file or folder, and Upload Files is FileUp so it pairs with Upload Folder's FolderUp ([7216b970](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/7216b970972afea483f31fc4e3ad22630c7b8913))
- make the CentOS and openSUSE distro icons readable on a dark background: CentOS was the one-color mark in its darkest navy and openSUSE the SUSE corporate chameleon in deep pine, about 1.3:1 against a dark theme, while every other icon is above 2.2:1; CentOS is now its official four-color pinwheel and openSUSE its own circle mark in its brand green, which also matches the name it is shown under ([ec12966a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/ec12966a3c8bd692ac971d9e0469dba88ee217af))
- make the ring the default working animation, since the loading spinners now take it and the ring is closest to the arc they showed before, and say under Settings > Appearance that every loading spinner uses the working animation ([d2a08273](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d2a082735119171bc4d1604e490d2a8d7bbc9cbc))
- show every loading spinner in the AI agent's working animation: the 44 Loader2 and LoaderCircle icons become Spinner, and the three refresh buttons that spun their icon show a Spinner while loading; a button that holds a Spinner keeps the narrower padding it has for an icon, so it does not widen while busy, and ESLint now refuses lucide's loader icons ([8dc1ccee](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/8dc1ccee0d83a99f23dec3fe5f10073c5f6f5f33))

### Other changes

- drop the comparison table from the READMEs: ranking tTerm against other clients reads as talking them down, and the reasons to choose tTerm already stand on their own ([3d26e7db](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3d26e7dbe5ccb2dacb8b06da7b40721c9f66caae))
- rewrite the READMEs to sell tTerm and move developer docs to CONTRIBUTING.md: visitors decide in seconds, but the first screen was a long feature list with the download link 200 lines down, so it now opens with the pitch, badges and download, then the reasons to switch, a comparison with Xshell, SecureCRT, Termius and Tabby checked against their public docs, install steps per platform, the macOS fixes for the first-launch "damaged" block (quarantine removal) and the Keychain prompt after every update (no Developer ID), collapsible feature lists and a FAQ; build, scripts, architecture and release notes move to CONTRIBUTING.md, whose checks now match AGENTS.md and CI ([2981043e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2981043e433ea835ba4064080907c27ce6a67b56))
- sort serial ports with sort_by_key: clippy 1.99 on CI flags the sort_by that compared two natural keys as unnecessary_sort_by, and sort_by_key orders them the same way ([149ed8fb](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/149ed8fbf3e27eed53c05ad6650d31a638580a56))
- describe the AI coding agent integration in both READMEs: one-click hooks or plugins for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and pi, tab badges while an agent works or waits, notifications, use over SSH and tmux, and the badge settings; also link the License section to the new LICENSE file ([c20f9199](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c20f919915630803b12e47e1ae48d9e6bc09fd70))
- add the MIT LICENSE file the README already named, so GitHub detects the license, and declare it as "license": "MIT" in package.json, Cargo.toml and the Tauri bundle config, which writes it into the deb and rpm package metadata ([46e5393d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/46e5393ddb79512e660f377480a19fcd8e92d090))

**Full comparison:** [v0.6.0...v0.7.0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/compare/v0.6.0...v0.7.0)
